recent_commits.message: reproducibility_check: fix the eight faults behind "other" errors (#578)
recent_commits.body:
- a setwd()/os.chdir() call over several lines is taken out whole
- a folder given to list.files(), dir(), Sys.glob(), os.listdir(),
  glob.glob() and the like is rewritten to where the deposit holds it
- a path under the folder of a removed setwd() counts from the working folder
- a folder variable made with paste0("...") is recognised, every value it is
  given is rewritten, and it becomes the run folder when a pasted file is
  found by its name
- four more messages of text no longer read as a factor start the run with
  R's old default
- a program that prints its usage and reads arguments needs a person;
  optparse, argparser and docopt count as reading arguments
- JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS opens java.util to rJava under Java 21 (tested in the image)
- new outcome out_of_memory, also when a compiler ran out of memory

Tests added; their expectations were checked directly, the suite not yet run.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Version 0.4.3.4: reproducibility_check fixes for #575 (work in progress)
recent_commits.body:
Fixes for the scripts that stopped on a missing file in the BES run (#575):
- a path written into a script gets the same changed name as its copy
  (a colon in a folder name)
- a file the deposit holds in another folder is copied to where a script
  looked, and the script runs again (file_placed); sf and terra errors read
- of several files with one name, the copy outside another project's folder
  is chosen; a name still ambiguous is counted, not kept as written
- a script runs again each time it stops on a new file another script wrote,
  up to five times
- an empty file the listing reports is written when the host refuses it;
  empty archive members are kept; folders of uncopied files are made
- a path inside here() counts from where here() starts
- the failure reason comes from the error that stopped the script; a program
  that cannot be started is 'environment'
- the package library is writable while scripts run
- a renamed file is suggested when one name is the other plus a piece

The checklist section now guides authors under "How to make your code run
on another computer": one block per problem, with the scripts affected and
the steps to fix it, and says so when the cause cannot be established. The
per-script table no longer repeats this advice.

Tests added but not yet run.

recent_commits.message: Version 0.4.3.3: AsPredicted preregistrations through ResearchBox's API
recent_commits.body:
aspredicted_info(), and with it prereg_check, reads AsPredicted's
preregistrations through ResearchBox's API (get_aspredicted) when a
ResearchBox key is set, and AsPredicted's web page otherwise. After
AsPredicted's captcha the API is still asked. New columns AP_registered,
AP_anonymous, AP_secondary, and from the API AP_number, AP_status,
AP_authors_count and AP_bundle; a cache argument, off by default (#570).
Version 1.05 of AsPredicted's questions is read correctly. ResearchBox's
limits for AsPredicted are kept apart from its limits for boxes.

prereg_check names an AsPredicted link that could not be read, with the
reason, instead of counting an empty row. Without a ResearchBox key, its
report and aspredicted_info() say that the web pages were read and how
to set a key; api_key_status() also reports ResearchBox's limit for
AsPredicted, so the apps tell visitors when it is reached.

Two faults found by the test warnings: .url_decode() keeps a % that
starts no code, where URLdecode() dropped characters or stopped (six
places), and paper_write() makes a new folder before asking for its
full path.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Version 0.4.3.2: help text sits directly above its function again
recent_commits.body:
Three helpers added in 8760708c and 45f57797 (#568) were placed between a

code_read(), .repro_binary_kind() above .repro_content_sniff(), and the
Python import helpers above .repro_py_imported(). The next run of

come before the blocks; no line of code changed, and roxygenise() now
changes no file.

recent_commits.message: Drop the minor gridlines in grim_plot_rates()
recent_commits.body: * Rates between the quarters mean nothing, and debit_plot() drops them too.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Limit `grim_plot_rates()` between 0 and 1
recent_commits.body:
* The reference lines are segments from 0 to 1, drawn with annotate():
  geom_segment() with constant positions drew one copy per study.
* They are grey40, which is about as dark as the stacked grey50 copies
  looked.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Write "GRIM inconsistency" without a hyphen
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Recycle grim_granularity() arguments by the tidyverse rules
recent_commits.body:
* Base `*` recycled any length into any other, such as 2 into 4, silently.
* grim_items() gets the same check while it is deprecated.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Report n in grim_values() and grimmer_values()
recent_commits.body:
* case counts through n when x is a single value, which the docs now say.
* An undecidable row keeps its n, so it can be told apart from the others.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Compute the threshold's scale once per value set
recent_commits.body:
* grim_scalar(), grimmer_scalar(), and debit_scalar() called
  rounding_scale() two or three times per row, and grim_scalar() called
  check_sum_range_exact() for every row; together with the flag check, the
  exactness checks of this release made grim() about 40% slower. The scale
  is now computed once, and the sum check is inlined, calling the function
  only for the error. grim() takes 0.25 s for 10,000 value sets, against
  0.30 s before and 0.21 s before the checks.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: State the size limits in the help pages instead of NEWS
recent_commits.body:
* The limits on significant digits and sums were only in NEWS, where the
  "Numeric inputs" bullet quoted their formulas. ?grim now states them,
  ?grimmer and ?debit say what they refuse beyond, and NEWS points there.
  The GRIMMER limit for n from 2 to 4 is the new one, about 3e5; the old
  "4.7e7 to 6.7e7" had only held for sd_sample.

* ?seq_disperse said dispersion "can be any numeric vector"; it takes
  non-negative whole numbers, and drops zeros and repeats.

* A NEWS line described a missing string by the development state before
  it.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Abort in big() for a negative or infinite input
recent_commits.body:
* floor(x / 2^24) never reaches 0 for either, so big() would loop forever.
  No caller passes one today; this makes a future one an internal error.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Let empty data frames bind to mapper output, and reject added rows in the audits
recent_commits.body:
* bind_rows(out, tibble(x = numeric())) was an error, though it adds no
  rows. vec_rbind() passes the vec_ptype2() methods prototypes without
  rows, so a plain data frame is now only rejected when it is cast, which
  skips inputs without rows. Two mapper outputs are still compared in
  vec_ptype2(), where the error names both arguments.

* full_join() and rbind() add rows that the vctrs methods never see, and
  audit_seq() then read them under the first call's verdicts, as NA for a
  case beyond its record. audit_seq() and audit_total_n() now reject any
  case or group with more rows than the call recorded. Basic mapper output
  records no rows, so joins remain uncovered there; NEWS says so.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Write the bounds of the mean and the number of ones in full in debit_explain()
recent_commits.body:
* The product of n and a bound of the mean was printed as a double rounded
  to 15 digits, so debit_explain(0, 0.3, 899999999999999, 0, 1) said
  "0.5 * 899999999999999 = 450000000000000" next to a range ending at
  449999999999999. The bound itself was rounded to four places, as 0.0222
  for 0.02225. Both are now written out exactly from the numerators.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Prune GRIMMER's remainders with the mean known, and refuse large SDs below n = 5 sooner
recent_commits.body:
* With the mean known, the sums can cover every remainder modulo n, as
  with digits_x = 0, and then GRIMMER tried all of them:
  grimmer(5, 0.0001, 999999, 0, 4, 1) took 19 s. The pruning of remainders
  out of the SD's reach, until now only applied with the mean unknown, now
  applies there too, and the case takes 0.08 s. 211,200 small-n
  brute-force cases and 6,000 random cases with n up to 5000 get the same
  verdicts as before.

* For n from 2 to 4, sums of squares from 2^40 on are refused, rather than
  from 2^52 or 2^53: deciding them took seconds and gigabytes for n = 3,
  13 s and 5.4 GB at an SD of 4.7e7. This rules out SDs of about 3e5 to 1e6,
  depending on n and sd_meaning, which no study reports for so few values.

* The too-large-n error writes n and the count in full, not as 2e+06.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Call .cols_derived functions once per mapper call, not once per row
recent_commits.body:
* grim_map() spent about three quarters of its time calling
  grim_exp_incon() row by row, 1.2 s of 1.6 s for 10,000 rows. The function
  is vectorized, and called once on the columns, it gives the same values;
  grim_map() now takes 0.36 s for those rows.

* .cols_derived is new in 1.0.0, so its contract changes without a
  deprecation: each function is vectorized, and a .reported_variadic
  argument comes as a list of each row's values.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Judge logical() like numeric() in is_seq_*() and use a repeated row once
recent_commits.body:
* is_seq_linear(logical()) was FALSE where is_seq_linear(numeric()) is
  TRUE; an empty logical vector is how R writes an empty vector of no type.

* row_to_colnames(row = c(1, 1)) pasted the row to itself, as in "x x".
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Raise scrutiny's own errors for list-columns, unnamed columns, and a list from
recent_commits.body:
* duplicate_count() failed in sort.int() on a list-column, and
  duplicate_tally() and duplicate_count_colpair() compared its elements as
  deparsed strings such as "1:3". All three now reject list-columns.

* duplicate_count_colpair() names unnamed columns by position, as the other
  duplicate_*() functions do; tibble rejected them.

* seq_disperse(from = list(1)) failed in is.finite().
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Reject a name repeated in constant
recent_commits.body:
* disperse(), disperse2(), disperse_total(), and the total-n mappers kept
  only the last of the columns that a repeated name in `constant` gave.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Refuse group sizes and dispersed values from 2^52 on
recent_commits.body:
* disperse2() took the mean of its two n values before any check, and from
  2^52 on that rounded the half away, so c(2^52 + 1, 2^52 + 2) gave wrong
  group sizes. All three disperse*() functions now refuse group sizes from
  2^52 on, one limit in place of 2^52 for halves and 2^53 for whole numbers.

* seq_disperse() checked decimal values against 2^53 units of their last
  place, where a double's spacing has long passed a unit, so
  "80000000000000.01" gave repeated values off the decimal grid. The limit
  is now 2^52 units, and the units are counted without dividing by `by`,
  which reported Inf for a tiny one.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Leave hits unknown in audit_total_n() that an undecided split might add to
recent_commits.body:
* A split whose both_consistent is NA might be a hit, so the hits of its
  direction and the total are NA, as audit_seq() has had it since 6f0f1b5.
  They were counted as misses.

* The audit sections of the sequence and total-n mappers now say that
  removed rows, as by filter(), make a count NA too.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Narrow the tolerance floor of is_seq_*() to two units in the last place
recent_commits.body:
* The floor of 8 * eps times the largest value, from 8306180, merged steps
  one unit apart in the 15th significant digit, so that
  is_seq_linear(c(9e14, 9e14 + 1, 9e14 + 3)) was TRUE. Steps and centers are
  off by at most two units in the last place, and such a step is at least
  4.5 of them. 30,000 generated sequences with 10 to 15 significant digits
  are now all judged right, linear and not.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Take n as a double in GRIMMER's candidate sums
recent_commits.body:
* With an integer n, as from read.csv(), the shift q * (s + r) overflowed
  once the mean was large, so grimmer_explain(), grimmer_values(), and
  explain_map() failed with a missing value where TRUE/FALSE was needed, and
  grimmer() warned. The verdict was unaffected.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Replace stray `ifelse()`s by `dplyr::if_else()`
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Let columns be added to mapper output again
recent_commits.body:
* Since a67f24d, bind_cols(), tidyr::nest(), and group_modify() on mapper

  given one value per row, reached the re-tests of its sequence or total-n
  mapper unchanged and failed with an error about the number of rows they
  test. function_map() records these arguments, and both tiers now say that
  they take a single value, as the sequence tier does for digits_*.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Say NA in the audits for any group with rows filtered out
recent_commits.body:
* audit_seq() only noticed a variable removed from every case, and counted
  hits of a variable removed from one case, or in part, as by
  filter(diff_var > -3), among the rows left. Sequence output now records
  the rows of each case's dispersion of each variable, and a group with
  fewer has unknown hits.

  audit(.by = dir), with totals and a rate of one direction alone. Total-n
  output records its rows per case and direction in the same way.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Raise scrutiny's own errors for more bad arguments
recent_commits.body:
* grim_plot_grid() checks that digits is a number and tile_size a single
  positive number; NA, "2", and "a" failed with R's own errors.
* seq_disperse() rejects an infinite offset_from, which failed in if ().
* The duplicate_*() functions reject repeated column names, which tibble
  rejected with an error of its own.
* split_by_parens(end1, end2), row_to_colnames(collapse), and
  duplicate_tally(colname_end) must be single strings: a vector failed in
  dplyr or was recycled, and NA was pasted in as "NA".

recent_commits.message: Refuse halves from 2^52 on in disperse() and disperse_total()
recent_commits.body:
* An odd total is split around a half, such as 2^52 - 1.5, and dispersed
  from there by disperse2(). From 2^52 on, a double holds no halves, so the
  pairs of disperse_total(2^53 - 3) added up to one less than the total.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Compare identical records first when binding mapper output
recent_commits.body:
* Binding the pieces of one sequence output compared its recorded values
  and verdicts element by element for every pair, which took 4 times as long
  for 1,445 pieces and grew quadratically. Pieces share one record, which
  identical() recognizes at once.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Update the stated limits of GRIMMER
recent_commits.body:
* NEWS still said grimmer() refuses sums of squares from 2^53 on, which it
  has computed exactly since big() numbers. The SD it refuses for n from 2
  to 4 is 4.7e7 to 6.7e7, divided by items_averaged, not some 4e7.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Count exactly in grim_total() where the products pass 2^53
recent_commits.body:
* With percent = TRUE and digits_x of 14, a rounding offset times n passed
  2^53, so the count of inconsistent values could be off by one although it
  was below 2^53 itself. Those elements now go through
  floor_product_ratio().
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Take gcd()'s steps with a large quotient in big numbers
recent_commits.body:
* A rounding bound over a denominator such as 10^17 made %% warn about a
  loss of accuracy, which it can really lose where long doubles are no wider
  than doubles, as on arm64. Such a step is now exact.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Show DEBIT's products exactly in debit_explain()
recent_commits.body:
* Past 2^53, n * (n - 1) and the denominators were printed as doubles,
  which show a neighbor of the true number, and the largest or smallest SD
  was picked among spreads that doubles tie, naming the wrong k. The k is
  now picked by its distance from n / 2, and the products are written out
  with the exact whole-number helpers.

recent_commits.body:
Batch of fixes from a two-model check of 10 never-processed psychology papers and
from defects reported by downstream consumers. See CHANGELOG [Unreleased].

Normalization
- extract_pdf runs one pdftotext -bbox pass (restore_line_end_hyphens=True) so
  plain-text callers get the layout-gated hyphen restores; a failed pass is
  recorded as line_end_hyphen_words_unavailable.
- W0v restores a hyphen inside a DOI broken at a line end; W0t handles compounds
  of three or more parts; W0u adjacency fix.
- S6u rejoins a URL or DOI broken across a line; capital-initials and list
  numbers keep the break. A list number is no longer glued onto the previous DOI.
- S0h keeps hyphens in documents whose font encodes the printed hyphen as U+00AD
  (document-level gate).
- P0t strips running titles repeated on later pages, publisher watermark
  sentences and "Downloaded from" stamps; ORCID URLs and supplementary-material
  body lines are kept.

Tables
- fields_raw on every flattened record (printed tokens).
- Typed descriptive pairs (M (SD), b (SE), n (%), est [CI]) with fields["group"]
  per arm column; new keys SE, count, pct.
- Nested spanning headers are not read as arm groups.
- Caption, label and running-head rows leave the grid for the caption; text-only
  tables keep their data rows out of the header.
- A captionless page directly continuing the previous table is linked
  (continuation_of, caption_status "continuation").

Sections and references
- Reference numbers separated from their entries are paired back via layout.
- Group, bare-surname and full-first-name authors start their own entry.
- A wrapped "Supplemental Materials." no longer opens a false section; an
  unheaded abstract of 1200-1500 characters is kept.

Tests: 4309 passed. Snapshot checksums re-pinned for 11 fixtures after verifying
every changed line is a hyphen insertion. 125-paper render diff reviewed: no
statistic lost.

recent_commits.message: Label-based multi-study isolation in production
recent_commits.body:
Isolation now defaults to the label method prototyped in
benchmarks/parser_eval/study_labels.py: one experiment-model call labels
every paragraph and sentence of the paper by study (labels only, no
text), and the target study's text is assembled deterministically from
the paper's own sentences (shared + target units, in order). Text is
verbatim, so nothing is paraphrased or dropped by regeneration; sentences
imported through a cross-reference carry a short
'[From Study X, cited for: <aspect>]' prefix, and the judge prompt now
says the target's own text takes precedence over imported lines.

New backend/services/study_labels.py holds the pure parts: a segmenter
that also handles PDF text layers (hard wraps, no blank lines, heading
lines, tables), the labelling prompt, label validation, target matching
("2" / "Study 2" / "Experiment 2" / single-study papers) and the filter.
On the CLI the labels are cached per paper, so every study of a paper
reuses one labelling call.

extract_experiment_specific_paper_text dispatches by method
(ISOLATION_METHOD, default labels) and falls back to the generative
rewrite when labelling fails; results and Redis record
multi_study_isolation_method and the fallback reason. Multi-study and
supplement runs now build the paper evidence from the original document,
with isolated chunks placed on its pages by word alignment.
recent_commits.author: Jamie Cummins

recent_commits.message: One canonical text per document
recent_commits.body:
The selected parser's output is now the single text the judge, retrieval
and the evidence text pane use. Previously, whenever the evidence viewer
was built (every web run), PDFs were re-chunked from PyMuPDF's text
layer and that text replaced the parser output, so GROBID/DPT2/bibr
results never reached the judge and partially scanned PDFs lost their
OCR. build_pdf_evidence_source now chunks the parser text and places each
chunk on the pages by aligning its words to the PDF word stream
(_DocumentWords: tolerant of running heads, page numbers and page
breaks); unplaceable chunks carry no offsets so the viewer searches
instead. Without parser text the text layer stays canonical.

Corpora built without the evidence viewer (plain CLI, eval scripts,
lazy builds in run_comparison) now use corpus_segments, the same
chunking, display normalisation and reference flags as the evidence
builder, so both paths embed identical segments. PDF registrations get
the same clean_document_text pass as other formats; number-only lines
are dropped only for PDF-derived text (an OSF answer of "300" was being
deleted). Corpus truncation at MAX_EMBEDDING_SEGMENTS is now logged.
recent_commits.author: Jamie Cummins

recent_commits.message: Judge independent dimensions in parallel
recent_commits.body:
All three orchestrators now dispatch dimensions through one helper,
_judge_dimensions. Without --append-previous-output the dimensions are
independent and run concurrently (DIMENSION_CONCURRENCY, default 4, per
job); partial and final results stay in dimension order. With the append
chain they run strictly in sequence as before.

Corpora are built once before fan-out (_ensure_text_corpora), which also
stops consensus strands from embedding the same documents once per
voter; the lazily-built full-paper corpus is guarded by a lock. Because
parallel threads write relevance scores into the shared evidence
manifest, it is persisted once after the dimensions finish (and per
dimension only in the sequential case).
recent_commits.author: Jamie Cummins

recent_commits.message: Worker: oldest-first queue, independent heartbeat, evidence off the loop
recent_commits.body:
Producers now LPUSH and the worker keeps popping the tail (BRPOPLPUSH),
so jobs run first-in-first-out; jobs reclaimed from a dead worker are
RPUSHed to the tail and run next. The heartbeat is refreshed by its own
task every TTL/3 instead of once per dequeue iteration, which stalled
while all job slots were busy and let a peer reclaim (and re-run) live
jobs. The orchestrators' synchronous evidence building and corpus
embedding now run via asyncio.to_thread so they no longer block the
event loop (and with it the heartbeat and other jobs).
recent_commits.author: Jamie Cummins

recent_commits.message: Keep supplements out of the references section; fix label-not-found framing
recent_commits.body:
Supplementary material appended after a paper's reference list was
flagged in_references and dropped from retrieval, disabling --supplement.
The references span now ends at the next merged-document separator
(DOCUMENT_SEPARATOR_RE), in both the evidence-builder flags and the
heading fallback in _reference_chunk_ids, and the separator line is a
chunk boundary.

For label_not_found_full_text runs the judge was told the paper reports
several studies and was pre-filtered; it now gets a variant that says the
label is absent, the excerpts are unfiltered, and the paper may report a
single study.

recent_commits.message: Surface supplement references; add --supplement to the CLI
recent_commits.body:
Detect references to supplementary material in the paper body
(supplement/supplemental/supplementary, supporting information, online
material[s]; the trailing reference list is ignored) and record
paper_references_supplement plus up to three matched snippets
(paper_supplement_mentions) on the result. When the paper points to a

recent_commits.message: Readable JATS tables; isolation retains footnotes and table notes
recent_commits.body:
extract_text_from_xml now emits one line per <tr> with cells joined by
' | ' (block tags inside a cell become spaces), drops layout whitespace
between table elements, and keeps <label>/<caption> before the table
body and table-wrap-foot notes after it. The isolation prompt explicitly
retains footnotes, table notes, captions, table contents and author
notes attached to included content; bumps _ISOLATION_PROMPT_VERSION.
recent_commits.author: Jamie Cummins

recent_commits.message: Ask the judge for likely alternatives; guarantee a semantic floor
recent_commits.body:
The unlocated_in_* instructions now ask for synonyms AND the most likely
alternatives a deviating document would state instead (pairwise ->
listwise, Prolific -> MTurk), which the literal scan searches. Term
parsing accepts comma/semicolon/'or' separators, keeps parenthesised
semicolons inside one element, and folds hyphens. _targeted_element_search
returns the top semantic hits even below the threshold when the literal
scan finds nothing, and reserves slots so literal hits are not crowded
out by scored semantic hits.
recent_commits.author: Jamie Cummins

recent_commits.message: Targeted verification searches the true full paper
recent_commits.body:
When multi-study isolation trimmed the paper, thread the pre-isolation
text into run_comparison and build a lazily-created, cached FULLPAPER_
corpus used only by _targeted_element_search for paper-side elements,
so footnotes and sections dropped by isolation stay reachable. Hits
already shown to the judge are de-duplicated by text containment;
hits from outside the isolated text are prefixed with
[outside the isolated target-study text] and the block explains how to
weigh them. Registration-side searches and reference-chunk exclusion are
unchanged.
recent_commits.author: Jamie Cummins

recent_commits.message: Isolation quality gate with full-text fallback and label pre-check
recent_commits.body:
Reject refusal-shaped or near-empty isolation output (shorter than
max(2000 chars, 5% of the paper), capped at half the source), never cache
it, and fall back to the full paper with multi_study_isolation=
"fallback_full_text". Skip isolation entirely when the study label (or a
Study/Experiment variant) never occurs in the paper
("label_not_found_full_text"). Multi-pass ensembles drop refused drafts
before the union. The isolation status is mirrored onto ComparisonResult
and the CLI batch summary so Redis-less runs can detect it; the report
banner covers the new statuses. Bumps _ISOLATION_PROMPT_VERSION.

10.1111/1365-2435.14173 stop with 'no lines available in input'.
highlights.author: Lakens

highlights.message: reproducibility_check: Python 2 code runs with Python 2.7 in Docker (#568)
highlights.body:
Scripts recognised as Python 2, and scripts that stop on a Python 2 module
they import, run again in python:2.7-slim, with their packages in a library
of their own (pip there picks the last versions that support Python 2). The
code is not converted. The report and the modifications table (python2) say
so. Option metacheck.docker_image_py2; FALSE keeps the old outcome.
highlights.author: Lakens

highlights.message: reproducibility_check: programs may run from /tmp; Cairo's PDF device; a lost container is Docker's failure (#568)
highlights.body: rstan's compiled models and Rcpp::sourceCpp() could not be loaded from /tmp, which Docker mounts noexec. Plots go to Cairo's PDF device, which takes any font name (theme_ipsum()'s Arial Narrow). "error waiting for container" counts as docker_failed.
highlights.author: Lakens

highlights.message: reproducibility_check: corpus fixes, round 3 (#568)
highlights.body: Model families are not fonts; package lists loaded through a function; absolute folders in variables get the deposit's folder; folders of writes in variables and file = are made; libraries in a Docker volume (INLA); archived dependencies first (ggsn); Stan syntax before 2.33 converted; Python programs with a window need a person; the run's echo no longer goes into sink() files (JAGS models); Git LFS pointers replaced by the deposit's copy; bare names read directly are found; here() no longer gets a .here in every run folder. Each change is reported.
highlights.author: Lakens

highlights.message: reproducibility_check: file names after the call, Windows paths, R's old defaults, files at the top (#568)
highlights.body: A file name on the line after its call is found (code_file_refs, repro_file_io). Quoted Windows paths get / before the run. A script that stops on text not read as factors (R before 4.0) or on Latin-1 data runs again with that default, as do the scripts waiting for its files. A path naming a file at the top as it is there counts from where the script runs. tidyhydat's database counts as needing the internet.
highlights.author: Lakens

highlights.message: reproducibility_check: scripts that stop on a file we did not download are not tried; Python installs on exFAT (#568)
highlights.body: A script that stopped on a file the deposit holds but that was not downloaded, mostly one over max_file_size, gets the outcome not_downloaded, is left out of the counted scripts and is counted in summary_table$repro_not_downloaded_n. pip installs inside the container and the result is copied to the library folder, since pip's own move copied permissions an exFAT drive refuses.
highlights.author: Lakens

highlights.message: Drop the minor gridlines in grim_plot_rates()
highlights.body: * Rates between the quarters mean nothing, and debit_plot() drops them too.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Limit `grim_plot_rates()` between 0 and 1
highlights.body:
* The reference lines are segments from 0 to 1, drawn with annotate():
  geom_segment() with constant positions drew one copy per study.
* They are grey40, which is about as dark as the stacked grey50 copies
  looked.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Write "GRIM inconsistency" without a hyphen
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Recycle grim_granularity() arguments by the tidyverse rules
highlights.body:
* Base `*` recycled any length into any other, such as 2 into 4, silently.
* grim_items() gets the same check while it is deprecated.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Report n in grim_values() and grimmer_values()
highlights.body:
* case counts through n when x is a single value, which the docs now say.
* An undecidable row keeps its n, so it can be told apart from the others.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Compute the threshold's scale once per value set
highlights.body:
* grim_scalar(), grimmer_scalar(), and debit_scalar() called
  rounding_scale() two or three times per row, and grim_scalar() called
  check_sum_range_exact() for every row; together with the flag check, the
  exactness checks of this release made grim() about 40% slower. The scale
  is now computed once, and the sum check is inlined, calling the function
  only for the error. grim() takes 0.25 s for 10,000 value sets, against
  0.30 s before and 0.21 s before the checks.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: State the size limits in the help pages instead of NEWS
highlights.body:
* The limits on significant digits and sums were only in NEWS, where the
  "Numeric inputs" bullet quoted their formulas. ?grim now states them,
  ?grimmer and ?debit say what they refuse beyond, and NEWS points there.
  The GRIMMER limit for n from 2 to 4 is the new one, about 3e5; the old
  "4.7e7 to 6.7e7" had only held for sd_sample.

* ?seq_disperse said dispersion "can be any numeric vector"; it takes
  non-negative whole numbers, and drops zeros and repeats.

* A NEWS line described a missing string by the development state before
  it.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Abort in big() for a negative or infinite input
highlights.body:
* floor(x / 2^24) never reaches 0 for either, so big() would loop forever.
  No caller passes one today; this makes a future one an internal error.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Let empty data frames bind to mapper output, and reject added rows in the audits
highlights.body:
* bind_rows(out, tibble(x = numeric())) was an error, though it adds no
  rows. vec_rbind() passes the vec_ptype2() methods prototypes without
  rows, so a plain data frame is now only rejected when it is cast, which
  skips inputs without rows. Two mapper outputs are still compared in
  vec_ptype2(), where the error names both arguments.

* full_join() and rbind() add rows that the vctrs methods never see, and
  audit_seq() then read them under the first call's verdicts, as NA for a
  case beyond its record. audit_seq() and audit_total_n() now reject any
  case or group with more rows than the call recorded. Basic mapper output
  records no rows, so joins remain uncovered there; NEWS says so.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Write the bounds of the mean and the number of ones in full in debit_explain()
highlights.body:
* The product of n and a bound of the mean was printed as a double rounded
  to 15 digits, so debit_explain(0, 0.3, 899999999999999, 0, 1) said
  "0.5 * 899999999999999 = 450000000000000" next to a range ending at
  449999999999999. The bound itself was rounded to four places, as 0.0222
  for 0.02225. Both are now written out exactly from the numerators.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Prune GRIMMER's remainders with the mean known, and refuse large SDs below n = 5 sooner
highlights.body:
* With the mean known, the sums can cover every remainder modulo n, as
  with digits_x = 0, and then GRIMMER tried all of them:
  grimmer(5, 0.0001, 999999, 0, 4, 1) took 19 s. The pruning of remainders
  out of the SD's reach, until now only applied with the mean unknown, now
  applies there too, and the case takes 0.08 s. 211,200 small-n
  brute-force cases and 6,000 random cases with n up to 5000 get the same
  verdicts as before.

* For n from 2 to 4, sums of squares from 2^40 on are refused, rather than
  from 2^52 or 2^53: deciding them took seconds and gigabytes for n = 3,
  13 s and 5.4 GB at an SD of 4.7e7. This rules out SDs of about 3e5 to 1e6,
  depending on n and sd_meaning, which no study reports for so few values.

* The too-large-n error writes n and the count in full, not as 2e+06.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Call .cols_derived functions once per mapper call, not once per row
highlights.body:
* grim_map() spent about three quarters of its time calling
  grim_exp_incon() row by row, 1.2 s of 1.6 s for 10,000 rows. The function
  is vectorized, and called once on the columns, it gives the same values;
  grim_map() now takes 0.36 s for those rows.

* .cols_derived is new in 1.0.0, so its contract changes without a
  deprecation: each function is vectorized, and a .reported_variadic
  argument comes as a list of each row's values.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Judge logical() like numeric() in is_seq_*() and use a repeated row once
highlights.body:
* is_seq_linear(logical()) was FALSE where is_seq_linear(numeric()) is
  TRUE; an empty logical vector is how R writes an empty vector of no type.

* row_to_colnames(row = c(1, 1)) pasted the row to itself, as in "x x".
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Raise scrutiny's own errors for list-columns, unnamed columns, and a list from
highlights.body:
* duplicate_count() failed in sort.int() on a list-column, and
  duplicate_tally() and duplicate_count_colpair() compared its elements as
  deparsed strings such as "1:3". All three now reject list-columns.

* duplicate_count_colpair() names unnamed columns by position, as the other
  duplicate_*() functions do; tibble rejected them.

* seq_disperse(from = list(1)) failed in is.finite().
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Reject a name repeated in constant
highlights.body:
* disperse(), disperse2(), disperse_total(), and the total-n mappers kept
  only the last of the columns that a repeated name in `constant` gave.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Refuse group sizes and dispersed values from 2^52 on
highlights.body:
* disperse2() took the mean of its two n values before any check, and from
  2^52 on that rounded the half away, so c(2^52 + 1, 2^52 + 2) gave wrong
  group sizes. All three disperse*() functions now refuse group sizes from
  2^52 on, one limit in place of 2^52 for halves and 2^53 for whole numbers.

* seq_disperse() checked decimal values against 2^53 units of their last
  place, where a double's spacing has long passed a unit, so
  "80000000000000.01" gave repeated values off the decimal grid. The limit
  is now 2^52 units, and the units are counted without dividing by `by`,
  which reported Inf for a tiny one.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Leave hits unknown in audit_total_n() that an undecided split might add to
highlights.body:
* A split whose both_consistent is NA might be a hit, so the hits of its
  direction and the total are NA, as audit_seq() has had it since 6f0f1b5.
  They were counted as misses.

* The audit sections of the sequence and total-n mappers now say that
  removed rows, as by filter(), make a count NA too.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Narrow the tolerance floor of is_seq_*() to two units in the last place
highlights.body:
* The floor of 8 * eps times the largest value, from 8306180, merged steps
  one unit apart in the 15th significant digit, so that
  is_seq_linear(c(9e14, 9e14 + 1, 9e14 + 3)) was TRUE. Steps and centers are
  off by at most two units in the last place, and such a step is at least
  4.5 of them. 30,000 generated sequences with 10 to 15 significant digits
  are now all judged right, linear and not.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Take n as a double in GRIMMER's candidate sums
highlights.body:
* With an integer n, as from read.csv(), the shift q * (s + r) overflowed
  once the mean was large, so grimmer_explain(), grimmer_values(), and
  explain_map() failed with a missing value where TRUE/FALSE was needed, and
  grimmer() warned. The verdict was unaffected.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung
